---
title: "Development"
---

For changes to JAXCMR itself, use the optional repository checkout described in
[Local setup with VS Code](developer-setup.ipynb). Run these commands from the
repository root.

## Prepare the environment

```bash
uv sync --locked --extra test --group reader
```

This installs the editable library, development tools, and notebook-test dependencies
in one environment. The `test` extra adds only pytest. The default `dev` group includes
the build and notebook tools for optional local checks; library CI does not install
that group. Optional groups remain available: `--group embeddings` for
sentence-transformers, `--group profiling` for line-profiler, and
`--extra experimental` for the experimental Numba helper.

## Edit and check notebooks

Edit original notebooks in `templates/` or `guide/`, preserving useful saved outputs.
Their short installation cells run only in Colab. Local and Slurm kernels use the
environment the reader selected.

While changing executable code, run the affected cases:

```bash
uv run --no-sync python guide/tools/check_notebooks.py --select cat_recall_rate
```

Run all 17 cases before publishing changes to shared setup, example inputs, or library
functionality:

```bash
uv run --no-sync python guide/tools/check_notebooks.py
```

The runner uses nbmake and pytest with two workers in the current environment. It
executes temporary notebook copies, reduces workloads for testing, and reopens saved
results in a separate process. The spreadsheet case uses synthetic inputs. Original
notebook parameters and outputs are never rewritten. `--jobs 1` runs serially;
`--platform windows` selects the representative Windows cases. The report identifies
the environment used and separates preparation and execution time.

Notebook execution is a local maintainer tool; GitHub Actions does not run notebooks
or tests that execute notebook cells.

For prose and saved-output changes, render and check the website; execution is needed
when calculations change. Adding a published notebook also requires adding its bounded
case to the notebook test runner.

## Test the library and installation

```bash
uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests -m "not audit" \
  --ignore=tests/test_distribution.py \
  --ignore=tests/test_reader_checks.py \
  --ignore=tests/test_template_adaptation.py \
  --ignore=tests/test_documentation.py
```

While editing, select the relevant test file instead of repeating the full suite.
Routine checks include scientific calculations, public validation, and complete modeling
workflows. Two additional `audit` cases check compilation reuse across prepared participant
selections in the experimental gradient and evolutionary CMR fitters:

```bash
uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests -m audit
```

Run these checks before releases and when changing experimental CMR preparation or fitting compilation.

Ordinary fitting uses `LossFn` with explicit trial indices. OptimizedCMR's
prepared observations and selection cache belong in
`jaxcmr/experimental/optimized_cmr.py`; its fitting adapters belong in
`jaxcmr/experimental/optimized_cmr_fitting.py`. Keep their types and preparation
methods out of the ordinary model/loss protocols. The ordinary optimizer
routines accept numerical objectives and are shared without importing the
experimental implementation.
Unfiltered pytest still includes the audit, notebook-related and distribution tests.
Routine CI runs only the library selection above, against a normal installation made
with `python -m pip install ".[test]"`. It uses `python -P -m pytest` so Python does not
import the adjacent checkout in place of the installed package. This tests dependency
resolution from the package requirements; local editable development still uses `uv.lock`.

The optional local distribution tests build a wheel and source archive, rebuild from the archive,
and install into a clean environment outside the checkout. They check the installed
README example and offline preparation of all bundled inputs. Library tests cover input
conflicts and custom paths; notebook checks exercise the current published notebooks.
This separate installation check needs internet access for dependencies and does not run in CI:

```bash
uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests/test_distribution.py
```

New tests should catch incorrect behavior using independently established numerical
answers or supported workflows. Put short derivations beside analytic expectations;
identify historical regression values as such. Check observable results rather than
private object identities, and use small doubles only at necessary boundaries. Required
checks must not silently skip because private data is unavailable. When an assertion's
strength is uncertain, temporarily introduce the suspected fault and confirm that it fails
for the intended reason. Keep the behavioral assertion, without adding a permanent test
that reruns another test. Test our notebook preparation and result validation directly;
rely on nbmake and pytest for notebook execution and failure reporting.

See the [test fixtures](https://github.com/githubpsyche/jaxcmr/blob/main/tests/fixtures/README.md)
and [CI workflow](https://github.com/githubpsyche/jaxcmr/blob/main/.github/workflows/tests.yml).

## Where shared operations live

Use `jaxcmr.dataset` for dataset construction, trial and recall selections, and
participant grouping. `jaxcmr.repetition` handles repeated items and shuffled
controls; `jaxcmr.math` contains numerical primitives. Shared figure creation and
the `save_figure` interface live in `jaxcmr.plotting`; analysis-specific plots stay
with their analyses.

`jaxcmr.analyses._study_positions` is private to the measurement analyses. It
computes presentation-inclusion masks and recall indicators; public analyses
own aggregation, weighting and interpretation. Keep measurement availability
separate from recall classification, including when an item appears repeatedly.
The operations in `repetition.py` return position indices for individual items;
the private analysis helpers return Boolean matrices over trials and positions.

The `jaxcmr.helpers` package contains general support modules: `io` reads and
writes the HDF5 array layout and loads JSON optimization settings, `paths`
resolves project directories and filenames,
`general` provides dotted-name imports and number formatting, and `figures`
implements figure saving. It does not import `plotting`, so plotting can use these
support functions without a circular import.

Library code imports directly from the module responsible for an operation.
Existing `from jaxcmr.helpers import ...` imports remain supported by explicit
re-exports in `helpers/__init__.py`; they do not contain separate implementations.
The package-level `jaxcmr.make_dataset` and `jaxcmr.load_data` imports also remain
available. `RecallDataset` and shared annotations stay in `jaxcmr.typing`.

`jaxcmr.fitting.parameters.bound_params` clips parameter columns to their bounds;
`jaxcmr.helpers.io.load_opt_params` reads fixed values and free-parameter bounds
from JSON. Their old imports from `jaxcmr.summarize` remain direct re-exports.
`summarize` owns descriptive parameter tables and statistical model comparisons,
not parameter preparation or file loading. Its small record types describe the
fields needed for reporting without requiring a complete optimizer result.

Declare type aliases with the Python 3.12 `type` statement. Use `Parameters` for
a mapping containing one set of scalar model settings; participant columns and
optimizer populations retain their explicitly shaped array annotations.

## Keep validation proportionate

Treat annotated types and shapes as caller responsibilities throughout the
library. Do not add runtime guards or tests solely to enforce those annotations.

Keep numerical functions focused on their calculations. Document valid input
shapes, codes and configuration; rely on ordinary array errors instead of repeating
shape, dtype and key checks in kernels. Valid inputs must compose with JAX
transformations, including numerical parameters passed through `vmap`.

Check fixed data at explicit preparation boundaries when needed to protect
participant assignment, prepared observations, saved-fit compatibility or file
integrity. Do not convert dynamic numerical arguments to NumPy for those checks.
Full distance preflight remains optional. Scientific eligibility masks, padding
and missing-observation rules stay in the calculation. Test supported numerical
behavior and demonstrated composition failures; remove tests for discarded guards.

## Maintain the supplied examples

The eleven selected files under `data/` and their fit methods document are the
authoritative inputs. Packaging explicitly includes them; other research data and
results remain excluded. The library’s `fetch_inputs(paths, base_dir=...)` copies
only requested bundled examples, reuses matching files, and preserves conflicts and
custom paths. An explicit `revision=` downloads reference bytes from GitHub on each call, including
when checking an existing file. The default bundled route works offline. Neither
route requires maintaining content hashes.

When changing a supplied input, update its methods or source notes as needed.
The filenames are listed in `jaxcmr/examples.py`; adding an example also requires
including it in the package configuration. `jaxcmr.examples.fetch_inputs` is the
current import; `jaxcmr.colab.fetch_inputs` remains compatible with older notebooks.
Reinstall the editable package to refresh its bundled resources, then run the notebook
and distribution checks:

```bash
uv sync --locked --extra test --group reader --reinstall-package jaxcmr
```

The website stages downloads from those same authoritative files. Notebook explanation
and analysis changes can be published without a package release. Library and bundled
data changes require readers to update their installation; the Git installation route
does not require a PyPI release.

## Saved settings and older notebooks

Fit and simulation records describe the models, parameters, input paths, selected
rows and run settings. Reuse checks compare these settings; fitting also recalculates
the saved objective. Changes to data or code at an existing location require rerunning
the affected calculations. Keep the input files and notebook with results you intend
to reproduce.

Automatic source capture and the former `jaxcmr.provenance` module have been
removed. Import `simulation_metadata_matches` from `jaxcmr.simulation`. Update
older notebook copies that import
`capture_notebook` or `file_sha256` from `jaxcmr.provenance`; those functions and the
`provenance_dir`, `provenance_source_paths` and `notebook_source` controls are no longer
used. Existing records can retain obsolete digest fields, which no longer govern reuse.

## Build and preview the website

Use [Quarto 1.11.9](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/tag/v1.11.9),
available on your command path, matching CI:

```bash
bash build-docs.sh
uv run --no-sync python guide/tools/check_site.py docs
uv run --no-sync python -m http.server 8786 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory docs
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8786/`. The build stages notebook pages and byte-for-byte source
downloads before rendering, without executing notebooks. It removes retired generated
files and protects source directories. Do not edit `guide/templates/`, `guide/downloads/`,
or rendered HTML. Rebuild after edits; the file server serves the rebuilt pages.

Colab links and installation commands follow `main`. A local preview’s download
includes local changes; its Colab button still opens the last pushed notebook.

## Publication and release handover

The routine **Checks and website** workflow runs on pull requests targeting `main`,
pushes to `main`, and manual requests. It has four testing/build jobs:

- **Library tests (Linux, macOS and Windows):** one shared job definition runs
  separately on all three platforms, using Python 3.12 and CPU execution. Each installs
  JAXCMR normally with `pip install ".[test]"`, then runs the same library tests and
  exclusions. A failure on one platform does not cancel the other platform runs.
- **Website:** a Quarto build, download/link checks, and a downloadable preview artifact.

Feature-branch pushes do not also trigger a second run for an open pull request.
Open a draft pull request to get automatic checks while working on a branch. There
is no file-based change selection; each routine run performs the four jobs.

CI does not execute notebooks, test notebook cells or run the separate distribution
rehearsal. The website build renders saved outputs and verifies download copies and links
without executing notebooks. There is no additional platform-compatibility workflow.
Notebook and distribution tools remain available for local use.

After the one-time Pages handover below, pushing documentation sources to `main`
builds and publishes the website automatically. Local rendering remains useful for
previewing changes; publishing no longer depends on committing generated HTML.
Pull requests produce downloadable previews without publishing them.

Deployment waits for the Linux, macOS, Windows and website jobs to pass, then publishes
the website artifact from that same run. It also checks that its commit is still the
latest `main`. A manual workflow run can publish `main` through the same checks.
No additional repository variable is required.

For the one-time handover:

1. Push the reviewed workflow and its supporting source changes. In repository
   **Settings → Pages → Build and deployment**, change **Source** from
   **Deploy from a branch** to **GitHub Actions**.
2. Run or rerun **Checks and website** for the current `main` commit, and verify that
   the library, website and deployment jobs all succeed. If branch rules require the
   previous job names, update those required checks when adopting this workflow.
3. Verify the public Setup pages, notebook downloads, example inputs, and Colab links.
   Check changed notebooks in hosted Colab separately, including a fresh runtime and
   your own input/output files.
4. After the replacement deployment is verified, remove `docs/` from Git tracking and
   add `/docs/` to `.gitignore`, keeping local rendered files available for previews.

Until the handover is completed, retain the tracked `docs/` site and the existing
branch-based publishing configuration. If the replacement deployment fails, the
previous public site remains available; fix the failure and rerun the workflow.

PyPI publication remains separate. Before publishing a release, review the library and
website checks, run the compilation audits, and select any additional local notebook or
distribution checks needed for the changes being released.
After publication, verify installation from
PyPI in a clean environment before changing the short installation commands. A PyPI
release is not required for ordinary notebook improvements or Git-based distribution.
